operationDefinition: Individual session web-search queries allocated to this five-paper batch; shared calls can include other batches. No direct page opens.

"Effect of Slag on the Strength and Shrinkage" "increasing"

review: Selected indexed primary passages, including primary abstract-level accounts. No complete PDF, visual, supplement, human/domain, full status or independent-dataset review claimed.

rights.access: Primary publisher/PMC passages through session web search; no access bypass.
rights.processing: Selected factual paraphrases and independent editorial guidance.
rights.rawRetention: No raw papers, abstracts, complete source tables or figures retained.
rights.aiTransmission: No separate external model service; analysis of session-exposed passages only.
rights.display: Original selected factual notes and independent planning, not replacement papers or reconstructed source tables.
rights.export: Same permitted original editorial fields as displayed.
rights.license: Exact full-text license/version remains unassessed. No protected source expression or assets reproduced.

provenance.title: Preparation and measurement
provenance.locator: Experimental design; strength and shrinkage methods

limitations: Retrieve water accounting, Na₂O denominator, sealing, test geometry and the matching source condition before scaling.
A strength maximum does not establish a minimum-shrinkage mix; keep drying and autogenous responses separate.
Selected primary passages only: complete outcome inventories, figures, supplements, sample uncertainty and source-status checks remain incomplete.

provenance.title: Selected outcome and boundary
provenance.locator: Abstract; mechanical results at 3, 7 and 28 days

limitations: Reconcile silicate solids, modulus, solution water, precursor proportions and curing before comparing Na/K chemistry alone.
Do not apply the reported flexure/compression proportions as a universal conversion or transfer the 28-day ranking to early strength.
Selected primary passages only: complete outcome inventories, figures, supplements, sample uncertainty and source-status checks remain incomplete.

provenance.title: Preparation and measurement
provenance.locator: Mix design; acid-exposure and characterization methods

limitations: Retrieve acid pH, renewal/control, exposure duration and comparison age before interpreting residual performance.
The shared acid container limits conclusions about cracks and individual leaching intensity; acid resistance is not interchangeable with unexposed strength.
Selected primary passages only: complete outcome inventories, figures, supplements, sample uncertainty and source-status checks remain incomplete.

provenance.title: Preparation and measurement
provenance.locator: Mixture optimization; printing and interlayer-tension methods

limitations: Retrieve nozzle geometry, layer interval, dose bases, direction and material water ledger before transferring the printable formulation.
Visual extrudability, directional compression and interlayer tension are different endpoints; printer settings and admixture adjustments are confounders.
Selected primary passages only: complete outcome inventories, figures, supplements, sample uncertainty and source-status checks remain incomplete.
Resolve duplicated activator wording in the abstract, exact source mix IDs and the optimized-versus-screening protocol before recipe transfer.
An orthogonal optimum is specific to factors and levels tested; concentration effects are not identical for Na and K systems.
Selected primary passages only: complete outcome inventories, figures, supplements, sample uncertainty and source-status checks remain incomplete.
